ops.title: Local `ty check` is a silent no-op — sessions inherit TY_CONFIG_FILE=.claude/ty-quiet.toml (all rules ignored); verify with `env -u TY_CONFIG_FILE`
ops.body:
Fleet sessions inherit `TY_CONFIG_FILE=.claude/ty-quiet.toml`, whose rules are `all = ignore`, so every `uv run ty check` is a silent no-op that always prints "All checks passed!" — a green local ty gate proves nothing. CI runs `ty` strict and catches the real errors. Reproduce CI's ty locally with `env -u TY_CONFIG_FILE uv run ty check <pkg>` (keep the `PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH` shim too).

This bit the cc-steer v14.5 migration: 32 real narrowing errors were invisible locally, red on CI. Shape: values read from `Mapping[str, object]` SQLite rows passed into typed sinks (TypedDict fields, `int()`/`float()`, typed method params) without narrowing — fix with `str(...)`/`int(str(...))`/`float(str(...))` matching sibling fields, narrow facade params to the platform's real types (SourceKind|None, VerdictLike, Fidelity), or fix a wrong return annotation to what's actually returned (e.g. `EventList`, not `list[TranscriptEvent]`). Note: `ty` does NOT honor mypy-style `# type: ignore[arg-type]`/`[misc]` codes — those were no-ops even before the poisoned config. See [[cc-transcript-build-env]].
